name: Abijah
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: The kings of Judah are set down in order from Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and on through the line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: He makes Abijah the son of Maachah chief and ruler among his brethren, intending to make him king, and he deals wisely by dispersing his children through the countries of Judah and Benjamin with abundant provision.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers, is buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Abijah begins to reign over Judah in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam the first. War breaks out between Abijah and Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Abijah sets the battle with 400,000 chosen men; Jeroboam answers with 800,000. Judah is outnumbered two to one, yet Abijah stands on the covenant of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Abijah pursues Jeroboam and takes cities from him. Jeroboam recovers no strength; the Most High strikes him and he dies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Abijah waxes mighty, marries fourteen wives, and begets twenty and two sons and sixteen daughters. His acts are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Abijah sleeps with his fathers and Asa his son reigns; the land is quiet ten years. Asa does that which is good and right, taking away the altars of the strange gods, the high places, the images, and the groves.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest
